Bring a clear request.
Leave with a traceable decision.

Use your own items and supplier offers. Compare what you actually need to purchase, inspect the source behind a number, and keep a review record tied to the version you saw.

Open your workbench

1. Build your purchase request

Choose Create a workspace, give it a title, and set its review date and currency. USD, EUR, GBP and VND are supported as separate workspace currencies. Each workspace uses one currency; the app does not convert currencies.

Under Purchase request, add the items you need. Each item has a label, a unique matching ID, a whole-unit quantity and a unit such as “ea” or “boxes”. You may also set a maximum lead time in days.

The matching ID connects an offer to the correct request item. Use exactly the same ID in your supplier CSV. You can edit the item later; changing its ID updates matched offers and the current selection inside the workspace.

For a quick tour, choose Open fictional example. Its suppliers, prices and purchasing request are synthetic and editable. The app is not restricted to those items.

2. Bring in supplier offers

Open Supplier offers. Use Add offer for manual entry or Import offers CSV to match your own column headings. A downloadable template includes your request item IDs.

For CSV import, map the required item ID, supplier, units per pack and price per pack. Optional columns can supply a quote ID, minimum packs, available stock packs, lead time, valid-through date, currency and delivery fee.

InputMeaning
Units per packHow many requested units one priced pack contains.
Price per packThe price of one whole pack. Use a dot decimal, no grouping or currency symbol, and at most two decimal places.
Minimum packs to buyThe supplier's minimum purchase quantity expressed in packs. The default is one.
Available packsTotal stock available for this line, measured in packs. Zero means unavailable; blank means unverified.
Delivery fee for this lineA one-time fee added to this offer line. It is not shared supplier-order freight. The default is zero.
Lead time / validityKnown facts checked against the item's constraint and the workspace review date. A valid-through date is inclusive.

If no currency column is mapped, the app explicitly uses the workspace currency. A mapped but blank currency is an error. Unmapped stock, lead time and expiry remain unknown. Supplied optional values are validated rather than silently replaced.

Import appends offers to the current workspace. A malformed structure, mapping or row rejects the entire import: no rows are silently skipped. Fix the error before importing again. Reimporting the same quote can create duplicate identities that must be resolved.

3. Compare the purchase you would make

The unit price is only one part of the decision. QuoteLens rounds to whole packs, respects minimum quantities and includes the line delivery fee.

Packs to buy = max(round up required units ÷ units per pack, minimum packs)

Line total = packs to buy × price per pack + line delivery fee

For example, 120 units in packs of 100 at 18.00 per pack require two packs: 36.00 before a line fee. Packs of 10 at 2.20 require twelve packs: 26.40. This is arithmetic on a fictional example, not a claim of customer savings.

Money is calculated exactly in integer minor units and displayed with two decimal places, including VND. Negative, grouped, exponent-form or over-precision prices are rejected instead of rounded or guessed.

Select Inspect source beside an offer to see its original fields and CSV filename and physical starting row. A manual offer shows its original entered fields and “Manual entry”. These values help explain the input; they do not authenticate what a supplier promised.

4. Read the checks before choosing

Blocked offers cannot authorize a completed selection. Reasons include insufficient known stock, expired validity, a missed lead-time constraint, wrong currency, invalid quantities or money, unmatched item identity and duplicate supplier/quote/item identities. Exact duplicate identities are also blocked; remove duplicates or use genuinely distinct quote references.

Eligible with warnings means the provided facts pass the checks, while some commercial facts remain unverified. Missing stock, lead time or expiry is not silently treated as confirmation. Unknown lead time blocks an item when that item has a maximum lead-time constraint.

In Compare & decide, choose an eligible offer for each request item. Select lowest eligible costs is a convenient starting point; you can choose another eligible offer and record a reason. Choose Save note after entering a reason, then wait for the saved state before reviewing. An incomplete selection shows a subtotal, not a completed approved total.

5. Record the reviewed revision

When every item has an eligible selection, choose Review this revision. Read the total, source values and unverified facts, then acknowledge the review. The approval records this exact workspace content and revision; it sends no order, payment or supplier message.

Changing a request, offer, selection, note or workspace setting requires another review. Earlier receipts remain in Decision history with their original inputs. The current decision can export an approved CSV and receipt JSON; historical receipts can be exported separately.

A receipt includes the selected lines, costs, source fields, reasons and a complete input snapshot. It is a local review record, not a signed purchase order, authenticated approval service or tamper-proof certificate. Spreadsheet formula-leading text is neutralized in exported CSV cells.

6. Keep a separate backup

Workspaces are stored in IndexedDB in this browser. The app reports whether a save succeeded. If it shows Not saved, keep the tab open and export a backup before closing.

Export backup saves one workspace, including history, to JSON. Use Import workspace backup to restore it. The file is validated before it is accepted; restoring a workspace with the same ID requires confirmation because it replaces the saved copy. Keep both files separately if you need two versions.

Deleting a workspace requires confirmation. The last deleted workspace can be restored during the same tab session. Browser storage is not a permanent archive: clearing site data, changing browsers or devices, or opening a different site origin does not carry your data across.

QuoteLens itself does not upload quote data, call an AI service, connect to suppliers or include an analytics SDK. It has no account, authentication or cloud sync. The hosting service still serves the page; local storage is specific to the origin where you use it.

What this version leaves to the reviewer

It does not read PDFs or images, perform OCR, infer missing supplier facts, convert currency, calculate taxes, aggregate shared supplier-order freight, place purchase orders or contact suppliers. Specification fit and commercial terms remain the reviewer's responsibility.

Practical limits are 200 request items, 2,000 offers, 64 CSV columns, roughly 2 MB of CSV characters, 8 MB of portable JSON characters and 50 receipts per workspace. Large history snapshots can reach the backup size limit first. Quantities are whole units; monetary inputs allow up to two decimal places.
